issues.description: download_and_untar.sh warns but does not exit when unzip is missing or archives are absent
issues.detail: When `unzip` is not installed the script only echoes a warning and proceeds; similarly, when an archive is missing it prints a message but returns 0. Downstream `local/data.sh` then runs `find` on non-existent directories and produces empty manifests, failing later with confusing errors. Invariant: if a precondition fails, terminate with non-zero status.

issues.description: Usage block in download_and_untar.sh prints help but does not exit on bad argv
issues.detail: The `if [ $# -lt 1 ] || [ $# -gt 2 ]` block prints usage but lacks `exit 1`, so the script continues with `$1` unset under `set -u` and aborts with an opaque `unbound variable` error instead of a clean usage failure. Terminate explicitly after printing usage.

issues.description: README link to ASR config is wrong (./conf/train/train_asr_branchformer_e24_amp.yaml)
issues.detail: The markdown link target is `./conf/train/train_asr_branchformer_e24_amp.yaml`, but the file actually lives at `./conf/train_asr_branchformer_e24_amp.yaml`. A reader following the link gets 404. Literate-programming hygiene: the documentation must point at the artifact it claims to point at.

issues.description: data.sh transcript-filtering pipeline has fragile invariant and clobbers utt.list mid-pipeline
issues.detail: `utt.list` is written from wav filenames, then later overwritten from `transcripts.txt` after filtering — but `filter_scp.pl` already consumed the first version. The invariant "utt.list = utterances surviving both wav discovery and transcript filtering" is implicit and not documented. Add a comment stating the invariant, or use distinct filenames (`utt.wavlist`, `utt.txtlist`) so the pipeline reads top-to-bottom.

issues.description: Character-normalization sed chain is opaque and incomplete; no comment states what set is being normalized
issues.detail: The pipeline strips `Ａ→A`, `#`, `=`, `、`, `，`, `？`, `。` and trailing spaces. No comment explains why these characters and not, e.g., `！`, `；`, `：`, full-width digits, or other full-width Latin letters. A reader cannot tell whether the list is exhaustive for the corpus or a partial cleanup. Add a one-line literate comment stating the normalization target.

issues.description: parse_options.sh is sourced before db.sh/path.sh/cmd.sh, but db.sh is required for the --downloads_dir branch
issues.detail: The current ordering parses CLI options first, then sources db/path/cmd. That happens to work because `TAL_ZH_ADULT_TEACH` is only read after sourcing, but the dependency is fragile and undocumented. A short comment stating the expected order of side-effects would help future readers.

review.summary: This is a standard ESPnet recipe addition — mostly configuration, symlinks, and a data-preparation shell script. The algorithmic content is thin, so review focuses on shell-script rigor and literate clarity. The most serious issues are in `download_and_untar.sh`, which fails to exit on missing prerequisites and on bad argv, allowing downstream stages to proceed with empty data. `local/data.sh` works but its sed/awk pipeline carries implicit invariants and an undocumented full-width-character normalization set that a careful reader cannot verify. Verdict: UNDER-AUDITED on the data-prep scripts; NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT on the normalization step.
